general: Be ready and checked in before your tee time.
League play follows the weekly format posted on the homepage.
Closest-to-the-pin prizes are tracked on holes 4 and 7 unless posted otherwise.
Twos and prize winners are posted after results are confirmed.
Match play opponents are responsible for contacting each other and arranging match dates.
Completed match results should be reported to league scoring as soon as possible.
Respect the course, staff, league members, and pace of play.
weeklyScoring: Weekly scores and match results are separate workflows. A match result should only be entered when a match was actually played and reported.
Weekly points come from the official scoring workbook. The website should display those workbook results instead of recalculating or guessing them.
The workbook sums each player's hole-by-hole Stableford points for the week.
Stableford points are based on adjusted score versus par using the workbook's 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 point ladder. Worse than bogey scores 0.
handicaps: Weekly handicaps and handicap movement are calculated in the official league workbook from the weekly scoring sheets.
The website should show the current workbook handicap for each member, but it should not invent handicap movement from website data.
When standings are refreshed, handicap changes should be taken from the workbook results for that scoring week.
standings: Final standings drop each player's two worst played scoring weeks.
Use the number of available scoring weeks actually played by the league, then subtract two.
Examples: 24 scoring weeks uses each player's best 22 weekly totals; 22 scoring weeks uses best 20; 18 scoring weeks uses best 16.
matchScoring: A, B, and C Division matches use handicaps.
Take the handicap difference, multiply by 75%, then round to the nearest whole number. A .5 result and higher rounds up.
The higher-handicap player receives the resulting strokes.
Apply match strokes in this hole order: 2, 6, 5, 7, 1, 3, 8, 9, 4.
Example: a 12 handicap versus a 6 handicap is a difference of 6. Six multiplied by 75% is 4.5, so that rounds to 5 strokes on holes 2, 6, 5, 7, and 1.
Club Championship matches do not use handicaps. They are straight match play, with the lowest gross score winning each hole.
